meta.title: Acme Field Sales Assistant: follow-up after customer meetings
meta.appetite: Six weeks of two people. 21 effort days over two tracks fits inside it.
meta.in_thirty_seconds: Reps first see their finished meetings with drafted follow-ups and a CRM update preview. Then they send and apply them with their own approval. The manager gets a weekly view last.
meta.method_note: Every date on this page is derived from the start date and the dependencies. Nothing is typed into a card. Durations are declared by the engineering lead, not measured: Acme has no tracker history yet.
meta.fictional: Fictional example. Acme is not a real company; every person, number, date and system is invented to show the method.

epic.title: Follow-up after customer meetings
epic.plain: After a customer meeting, the rep reviews a drafted follow-up and a proposed CRM update instead of writing both from scratch.
sections: Late follow-ups are the most common reason deals go quiet, and reps lose time writing the same email and CRM note after every meeting.
Reps send a reviewed follow-up quickly, and the CRM stays current without manual entry.
Share of follow-ups sent within 2 hours of the meeting end.
Share of finished meetings with a current CRM update.
Share of drafts the rep sends without rewriting the facts.
Risk: drafts contain unsourced facts. Mitigation: eval set with a 100 percent pass mark on never-cases before phase 1 exit.
Risk: the CRM changes between preview and apply. Mitigation: re-read before write and stop on change.
Risk: reps ignore the list. Mitigation: show it as the first screen they open.

features.title: Meetings and notes
features.plain: The rep sees which meetings just ended and what was noted in each.
sections: List finished meetings of the day.
A finished meeting appears within 15 minutes of its end (finding A2).
A meeting with no notes is marked as such.

features.title: Follow-up draft and send
features.plain: The rep gets a drafted follow-up, edits it and sends it from their own mailbox.
sections: No fact outside the notes and the CRM.
Send only after an explicit rep action.

features.title: CRM write-back
features.plain: The assistant proposes the CRM update, shows it, and applies it only when the rep approves.
sections: Show old and new values with sources.
Every write re-reads the record first.

features.title: Activity trail
features.plain: The manager sees what the assistant suggested and what the reps did with it.
sections: Record every suggestion, send, apply and ignore with a timestamp.
Show counts per rep per week.
Counts reconcile with the trail for one week of test data.

stories.title: Show today's finished meetings with their notes
stories.plain: Each morning and after each meeting, the rep sees what happened in their meetings without opening three tools.
sections: As an account executive, I want to see my finished meetings with their notes so that I can review them in one place.
Without this list the assistant has nothing to draft from, and the rep keeps switching tools.
The rep opens the list and sees today's meetings with notes.
Each finished meeting appears with end time, attendees and a note excerpt.
A meeting without notes is flagged.
Only the rep's own meetings appear.
Calendar unreachable: show the last good list with its timestamp.

stories.title: Draft a follow-up email from the meeting notes
stories.plain: After a meeting, the rep finds a ready draft of the follow-up email with the facts it used listed beside it.
sections: As an account executive, I want a drafted follow-up so that I review instead of write.
The draft is the main time saving, and listing the facts is how the rep trusts it.
Open a finished meeting and read its draft with the sources shown.
A draft exists for each meeting with notes.
Each fact is listed with its source.
Notes too short: show a message instead of a draft.
Spec, capability follow-up-draft. Eval cases E01 to E06.

stories.title: Send the follow-up after the rep edits it
stories.plain: The rep edits the draft and sends it, and nothing is ever sent without that action.
sections: As an account executive, I want to send the follow-up from my own mailbox so that the customer hears from me.
This is the one action that reaches the customer, so it is the autonomy boundary that matters most.
Edit a draft, send it, and see it in the sent folder.
Send runs only after an explicit rep action.
The email leaves the rep's mailbox.
The sent email id is stored in the trail.
Mailbox error: keep the draft and show the error.
Spec, autonomy boundary "Ask first: send an email".

stories.title: Show a CRM update preview for a finished meeting
stories.plain: After a meeting, the rep sees exactly which CRM fields would change and why.
sections: As an account executive, I want a CRM update preview so that I can approve changes quickly.
The preview is what makes a write safe, and without it reps would not allow writes.
Open a finished meeting and see each field with old and new values.
Each field shows old value, new value and source.

stories.title: Apply the CRM update the rep approved
stories.plain: When the rep approves a preview, the CRM is updated, and if the record changed in the meantime the update stops.
sections: As an account executive, I want my approved update applied so that I do not retype it.
This closes the loop and proves the autonomy contract holds when the system writes.
Approve a preview and see the CRM change.
The record is re-read before the write.
The apply stops if the record changed since the preview.
The result is recorded in the trail.
CRM unavailable: keep the preview and retry later.
Spec, autonomy boundary "Ask first: write any field to the CRM". Built through the single write path described in the agent brief.

stories.title: Block the update when the contact has no CRM match
stories.plain: If a meeting attendee is not a contact on the deal, the assistant does not propose an update and says why.
sections: As an account executive, I want the assistant to refuse unmatched contacts so that it never changes the wrong record.
Writing to the wrong deal is the failure reps fear most.
Open a meeting with an unknown attendee and see the reason shown.
With no matching contact on the deal, no preview is offered.
More than one possible match: ask the rep to choose.
Spec, autonomy boundary "Never: contact anyone who is not already a contact on the deal".

stories.title: Show the manager what was sent, applied and ignored
stories.plain: The sales manager sees per rep, per week, how many suggestions were sent, applied or ignored.
sections: As a sales manager, I want a weekly activity view so that I can coach follow-up habits.
It is the measurement of the success criterion and the source for coaching.
Pick a week and see counts per rep.
Counts per rep for sent, applied and ignored.
A week with no data shows zero, not an error.

phases.name: See and draft
phases.goes_live: The rep opens a daily list of finished meetings, reads a drafted follow-up and sees a CRM update preview. Nothing is sent and nothing is written.
phases.why: It proves the data and the draft quality with no customer risk.
phases.exit_gate: A rep sees a draft and a preview for a real meeting, and the evals for "no invented facts" pass.

phases.name: Send and write back
phases.goes_live: The rep edits and sends the follow-up from their mailbox, and approves a CRM update that is then applied.
phases.why: These are the two actions that touch the outside world, so they come after the drafts are trusted.
phases.exit_gate: Probes confirm no send and no CRM write without approval, and the success measurement runs on the trail.

phases.name: Manager view
phases.goes_live: The sales manager sees sent, applied and ignored counts per rep per week.
phases.why: It reads the trail that phases 1 and 2 produce.
phases.exit_gate: Counts reconcile with the trail for one week of test data.

cadence.demonstrable: The daily list of finished meetings with notes.
Drafts and CRM previews for real meetings; the rep sends a follow-up.
Approving a preview writes to the CRM, and the manager sees the week.

exists.saves: No new integration work for US01
Safe testing of US04, US05, US06

touchpoints.depends: Mail admin must allow send as the rep

glossary.definition: The system where deals and contacts are recorded.
An email written by the assistant that the rep has not sent.
A list of CRM changes shown before anything is written.
The record of what was suggested, sent, applied and ignored.
The longest chain of dependent stories, which sets the minimum duration.
A group of stories that goes to production together, with its own exit gate.
The check a phase must pass before the next phase starts.
A written limit on what the assistant may do without asking.
A test of a probabilistic behavior against a set of real cases, scored as a pass rate.
One of the parallel lines of work in the schedule. A schedule assumption, not a staffing promise.

decisions.decision: Can the assistant read transcripts as well as typed notes?
Is a read receipt acceptable on follow-ups?
How long is the trail kept?

findings.finding: The CRM has two fields for deal value, and the spec names only one.
findings.effect: US02 and US04 must read the field the spec names. Confirm with sales operations before US02 starts.

findings.finding: The notes tool returns notes up to 10 minutes after a meeting ends.
findings.effect: The "appears within 5 minutes" criterion in F1.1 changed to "within 15 minutes" unless the notes tool is faster in production.

decided: The email is sent from the rep's own mailbox.
Customer success meetings are out of this slice.

tracker_order: The epic, then Features F1.1 to F1.4, then US01 to US07, then the dependency links, then the iteration assignment by phase. The tracker assigns its own codes at creation; the mapping from these ids to tracker codes is kept in the numbering register.
